items.title: 52263_Sonny Greer oral history interview
items.q: everybody's hollering, "Cootie, Cootie." So Cootie come up. He was home, boy.

ctx.x: So I fixed about six or seven of them, you know, they were so big, for myself. Man, after they got the hang of it, them crabs didn't last a minute. And the beer. Now they wanted to help me eat mine. I said, no way. No, no, no way. But that was a lot of good -- so we left there. The reason we left so late in the morning, we had to play in Mobile, Alabama the next night. So we left. So Cootie's home is in Mobile, Alabama. We pulled into Mobile, Alabama, I think it was -- no we played someplace else, I forget where…

And man, I was sleeping. I heard all this noise, I raised the little shade and saw all these people, I said, man, and everybody's hollering, "Cootie, Cootie." So Cootie come up. He was home, boy. So Duke came out, Duke put on a robe and came to the platform, hollered at us. I ain't never budged. So we played Mobile that night, packed, four, five thousand people. The white was spectators. You know, down there if the colored had the dance, the white people could come as spectators. But, you know, not dance. They…
So man, Duke or somebody say he liked watermelon.
